Summary from call:
- Target P95 latency: 75-100 ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens
- Sustained throughput target: ~120 reqs/min (burst to 300/min)
- Concurrency target: 50 concurrent sessions based on expected peak traffic
- Streaming: client requires token-level streaming for chat UX (low fanout)

Network specifics you shared:
- Primary path: Acme VPC peering to Redwood Transit VPC in us-west-2
- Secondary: IPSec VPN fallback to our SFO colo (egress through 3rd-party gateway)
- Expected inter-region RTT (app-to-serving): 12-18 ms internal (they will confirm)

Open items / asks for Acme Network Team:
1) Confirm peering CIDRs and whether BGP will be used or static routes.
2) Provide measured RTT and jitter numbers from app hosts to the SFO colo and to us-west-2.
3) Confirm egress NAT behavior and whether keepalive/idle timeout can be extended beyond 10 minutes.

Attached: redwood_vpc_requirements.pdf (our standard VPC checklist) and the mutual_action_plan.xlsx draft. I've copied Jordan for any additional performance questions.

- Follow-up meeting to review test results and finalize any config changes (target: next Wed).

Marissa - thanks for the summary, that matches what we discussed. A few notes from the network side:

1) Peering and routing - we plan to use VPC peering between Acme-prod VPC and Redwood Transit VPC. We will start with static routing; BGP is possible but would require change control with infra. CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/16 (Acme-prod), 172.31.0.0/16 (Redwood-transit).

2) Latency measurements - quick numbers from our internal probes (from app-hosts in us-west-2 to our SFO colo / Redwood transit):
   - App -> Redwood Transit (us-west-2): median RTT 14 ms, p95 26 ms, jitter 4 ms
   - App -> SFO colo (VPN path): median RTT 34 ms, p95 58 ms, jitter 12 ms

3) Egress/NAT - our egress gateway currently has a 15-minute idle timeout; we can extend to 60 minutes for long-lived streaming connections if required. NAT port preservation is supported.

4) Concurrency estimate - we can support 50 concurrent sessions from the app side without additional infra, but if concurrency grows to 150+ we'll need to provision extra app-tier capacity.

We attached a network diagram (acme_network_diagram.png) and I've asked the NetOps team to run a traceroute to the Redwood IPs during peak tomorrow to capture path variation.

Questions for Redwood:
- What concurrency limit per GPU instance do you recommend for streaming chat with 512-token contexts?
- Any specific TCP/TLS tuning (keepalives, window sizes) you recommend for the peered path?

Happy to jump on a call with NetOps and your infra/dev on Thursday morning PST.

- Tom Reyes

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification / Private VPC - follow-up (internal)

Quick internal notes based on Tom's numbers:

- App -> Redwood Transit p95 26 ms is good; adds to our processing time budget. With a 75-100 ms target P95 we need serve-side p95 token latency ~40-60 ms depending on model. For 512 tokens with streaming we should size for 40 ms token production at peak.
- Concurrency: for streaming chat we recommend starting with 8-12 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU (A100 80GB equivalent) depending on model family. If they want 50 concurrent sessions, that's ~5-7 GPUs reserved; include headroom for autoscale + burst.
- Throughput: 120 reqs/min sustained maps to ~2 reqs/sec - negligible for CPU but GPU-bound depending on prompt size. We should run a synthetic ramp using their peered path to model tail latencies.

Action items I can own:
1) Draft test plan for streaming + concurrency (include token-level timers).
2) Provide recommended GPU sizing and concurrency-per-GPU table for typical model families (gpt-like and instruction-tuned).
3) Prepare a small readout doc with TCP/TLS tuning suggestions (keepalive intervals, MSS, etc.).

I'll attach the test plan to the MAP. Planning a 30-45 minute run with 10 concurrent streams to validate p95.

- Aditya
